vendors.name: Unity Catalog
vendors.tagline: Databricks governance catalog for tables, metric views, models and MCP services, with an open source edition.
vendors.verdictNote: Unity Catalog stores metric views as governed objects, adds tags, domains and AI comments, and serves them to agents through governed MCP services.

artifacts.name: Unity Catalog metric views
artifacts.format: SQL DDL (CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS) or YAML 1.1; Catalog Explorer editor

artifacts.name: Tags and governed tags
artifacts.format: SQL, UI, REST API; governed tags enforce allowed keys and values

artifacts.name: AI-generated comments
artifacts.format: Catalog Explorer; the owner reviews each draft before saving

artifacts.name: Pages (governed business definitions)
artifacts.format: UI; Beta, enabled by an account admin

artifacts.name: Domains and subdomains
artifacts.format: UI; governed tags place assets in a domain. No stage label in docs

artifacts.name: Certified and deprecated flags
artifacts.format: System tag system.certification_status. No stage label in docs

artifacts.name: Data Classification
artifacts.format: Agentic scan that applies sensitivity tags to tables

artifacts.name: Lineage and lineage system tables
artifacts.format: Column-level lineage in UI and REST API; system.access.table_lineage and column_lineage

artifacts.name: Databricks-provided MCPs (Genie One MCP and others)
artifacts.format: Each MCP is a Unity Catalog securable behind Unity Gateway; some servers need the Unity Gateway beta

artifacts.name: Unity Catalog OSS metric views
artifacts.format: Open source server; metric view YAML stored through REST API and Spark. No stage label

metrics.n: Metric views hold measures as Unity Catalog securables. Standard privileges apply. Open source Unity Catalog also stores metric view YAML.

dimensions.n: Metric views declare dimensions as fields, with a join list. The docs do not describe hierarchies or time grains.

relationships.n: Metric view YAML declares joins and join cardinality. The catalog itself does not expose a separate relationship object.

synonyms.n: Comments, tags, and metric view synonyms are readable by agents. Pages add authoritative term definitions but are Beta.

verifiedQueries.n: Example SQL and trusted assets live in Genie Agents, not in the catalog. The catalog supplies certification flags only.

nl2sql.n: Genie One answers questions with Unity Catalog semantics. It is a separate Databricks product, not a catalog feature.

ontology.n: Domains and Pages form the human-modeled layer of Genie Ontology. Pages are Beta. No user-defined object or link types.

graph.n: No graph query language. Lineage is a graph in the UI and API, but users cannot run graph queries on business data.

vector.n: Vector search is a separate Databricks product that uses Unity Catalog governance. The catalog search is not documented as semantic search.

mcp.n: Databricks-provided MCPs are Unity Catalog securables. The Genie One MCP is GA. The SQL MCP needs the Unity Gateway beta.

governance.n: Grants, ABAC row filters and column masks, certification tags, audit logs, and lineage apply to tables and metric views.

openStandard.n: Open source Unity Catalog is Apache 2.0 with an OpenAPI spec. Databricks also exposes an Iceberg REST catalog endpoint.

aiDescriptions.n: Catalog Explorer drafts comments for catalogs, schemas, tables, columns, functions, models and volumes. Saving runs ALTER, which can disrupt jobs.

bulkMetadata.n: COMMENT ON, ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN and SET TAGS write metadata in SQL. REST API and SDKs also work. No file import tool.

autoClassify.n: Data Classification tags sensitive data on a schedule. Scanning views is Beta. Tags feed ABAC policies.

sampleValues.n: Value matching and sampling are Genie Agents features. The catalog does not sample values for AI.

queryHistory.n: Genie suggests example queries from workspace query history. The catalog itself only records lineage from queries.

lineage.n: Automatic column-level lineage across workspaces, a lineage API, external lineage, and system tables with a one-year rolling window.

evals.n: Genie benchmarks score a Genie Agent against reference SQL. This is a Genie feature, not a catalog feature.

offers: Metric views are governed catalog objects with standard grants, so agents see only what the caller can see.
Governed tags, domains, certification flags and Pages give an agent machine-readable trust and business meaning.
Catalog Explorer drafts AI comments for tables and columns that an owner can review and save.
Lineage system tables let an agent or a script query upstream and downstream tables with SQL.
Databricks-provided MCPs run under Unity Catalog permissions and grants.
The open source edition serves Iceberg REST clients and stores metric view definitions.
gaps: Pages are Beta, and the docs show no stage label for domains or certification flags.
The catalog does not store verified question and SQL pairs. Genie Agents hold them.
Natural language SQL, value sampling and evals belong to Genie, which is a separate product from the catalog.
The open source edition lists no AI comments, tags, lineage, or MCP server in its docs index.
AI comments need human review, and the docs warn against using them to detect PII.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Define metrics as metric views and add comments, tags and certification flags. Then connect the agent through the Genie One MCP server so it reads those definitions under the caller's permissions. Use the SQL MCP only for queries you already wrote.

snippet.title: Create a metric view in Unity Catalog
snippet.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW orders_metric_view WITH METRICS LANGUAGE YAML AS
$$
version: 1.1
comment: "Orders KPIs for sales analysis"
source: samples.tpch.orders
fields:
  - name: Order Month
    expr: DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', source.o_orderdate)
    comment: 'Month of order'
measures:
  - name: Order Count
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: 'Total number of orders'
$$

vendors.name: Snowflake Horizon Catalog
vendors.tagline: Snowflake built-in catalog for discovery, semantic views, lineage, governance and an Iceberg REST endpoint.
vendors.verdictNote: Horizon Catalog stores semantic views as schema objects and adds tags, descriptions, classification and lineage that Cortex and MCP clients read.

artifacts.name: Semantic views
artifacts.format: SQL DDL (CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW) or YAML; schema-level objects with grants and tags

artifacts.name: Semantic View Autopilot
artifacts.format: Snowsight wizard that drafts tables, relationships and metrics

artifacts.name: Auto-generated descriptions (AI_GENERATE_TABLE_DESC)
artifacts.format: Stored procedure and Snowsight; optional sample data

artifacts.name: Object tagging and Snowflake-provided tags
artifacts.format: SQL; tags inherit and propagate. SNOWFLAKE.TAGS.CERTIFICATION_STATUS marks trusted assets

artifacts.name: Sensitive data classification
artifacts.format: Classification profiles and Trust Center; Enterprise Edition

artifacts.name: Data lineage and GET_LINEAGE
artifacts.format: Snowsight graph and SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE; Enterprise Edition

artifacts.name: Metadata connectors
artifacts.format: Collect schemas, query logs and dashboards from PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI and dbt

artifacts.name: Horizon Iceberg REST Catalog API
artifacts.format: Iceberg REST endpoint for Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables; vended credentials

artifacts.name: Catalog-linked databases
artifacts.format: Sync Iceberg tables from an external Iceberg REST catalog, such as AWS Glue

artifacts.name: Snowflake-managed MCP server
artifacts.format: Tools for Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, Cortex Agents and SQL; RBAC per tool

metrics.n: Semantic views define metrics, including derived metrics, as schema objects with grants.

dimensions.n: Semantic views declare dimensions and facts on logical tables.

relationships.n: CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW has a RELATIONSHIPS clause that declares joins between logical tables.

synonyms.n: Semantic views take synonyms, comments, and the AI_SQL_GENERATION instruction text. Tags and table comments add more context.

verifiedQueries.n: The AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES clause stores question and SQL pairs inside the semantic view.

nl2sql.n: Cortex Analyst and Cortex Agents answer questions against semantic views. They are Snowflake AI products, not catalog features.

ontology.n: No object, link or action model. Semantic views, tags and certification status are the closest features.

graph.n: The catalog has a lineage graph in Snowsight. No graph query language for business data was found in the docs.

vector.n: Cortex Search is a separate service that a semantic view can use. Universal Search is not described as vector search in the docs.

mcp.n: The managed MCP server is GA and exposes Cortex Analyst on semantic views. The docs list no catalog-only search tool.

governance.n: Masking and row access policies apply to every caller. Tags, certification status, classification, and lineage cover semantic views.

openStandard.n: Horizon exposes an Iceberg REST Catalog API built on Apache Polaris. Semantic view YAML import is separate.

aiDescriptions.n: AI_GENERATE_TABLE_DESC drafts table and column descriptions, optionally from sample data. Snowsight has a matching UI path.

bulkMetadata.n: One ALTER TABLE ... ALTER statement sets comments on many columns. SET TAG and tag propagation scale tags. No file import tool.

autoClassify.n: Classification profiles tag sensitive columns automatically. The feature needs Enterprise Edition.

sampleValues.n: Semantic view dimensions accept SAMPLE_VALUES and IS_ENUM. Authors write the values; Snowflake does not sample them for you.

queryHistory.n: Horizon Context collects query history and popularity. Autopilot uses query history to suggest relationships and verified queries.

lineage.n: Column-level lineage from Snowflake, external databases, BI tools, and OpenLineage feeds. GET_LINEAGE accepts the SEMANTIC_VIEW domain.

evals.n: Cortex Analyst evaluations run a semantic view against verified queries. They are an AI product feature, not a catalog feature.

offers: Semantic views are schema objects, so grants, tags, sharing and lineage apply to them.
AI_GENERATE_TABLE_DESC writes table and column descriptions from metadata and sample data.
The SNOWFLAKE.TAGS.CERTIFICATION_STATUS tag gives agents a fixed trust signal for CERTIFIED and DEPRECATED assets.
The Horizon Iceberg REST Catalog API lets Spark and other engines read Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables under Snowflake roles.
Catalog-linked databases pull in Iceberg tables from an external Iceberg REST catalog, such as AWS Glue.
Column-level lineage covers Snowflake objects and OpenLineage feeds, and GET_LINEAGE returns it in SQL.
gaps: Metadata connectors for PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI and dbt are Preview.
The docs describe no business glossary object. Teams use tags and semantic view comments.
Writes through the Horizon Iceberg REST API and access to externally managed Iceberg tables are Preview in the release notes.
Lineage, tagging, and classification need Enterprise Edition or higher.
No ontology layer with objects, links or actions.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Create a semantic view over certified tables, add synonyms, comments and verified queries, and tag it. Then give agents access through the Snowflake-managed MCP server so Cortex Analyst reads the view under the caller's role.

snippet.title: Create a semantic view with a synonym and a verified query clause
snippet.code:
CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW tpch_rev_analysis
  TABLES (
    orders AS SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.TPCH_SF1.ORDERS
      PRIMARY KEY (o_orderkey)
      WITH SYNONYMS ('sales orders')
      COMMENT = 'All orders table for the sales domain',
    customers AS SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.TPCH_SF1.CUSTOMER
      PRIMARY KEY (c_custkey)
  )
  RELATIONSHIPS (
    orders_to_customers AS orders (o_custkey) REFERENCES customers
  )
  METRICS (
    orders.order_count AS COUNT(orders.o_orderkey)
  );

vendors.name: Amazon SageMaker Catalog and AWS Glue Data Catalog
vendors.tagline: AWS business catalog with glossary, data products and lineage, on top of the Glue technical catalog.
vendors.verdictNote: SageMaker Catalog gives descriptions, glossary terms, metadata forms and lineage to agents, but it holds no governed metric or join definitions.

artifacts.format: Console and DataZone API (CreateGlossary, CreateGlossaryTerm); terms hold synonyms and related terms

artifacts.name: AI recommendations for names, descriptions and glossary terms
artifacts.format: Amazon Bedrock; console and StartMetadataGenerationRun API; limited Regions and quotas

artifacts.name: Data products
artifacts.format: Group assets with metadata and one access request; CreateDataProduct API

artifacts.name: Data lineage
artifacts.format: OpenLineage compatible; automatic capture from Glue, Redshift and Spark; PostLineageEvent API

artifacts.name: AI classification with glossary terms (PII, PHI)

artifacts.format: Technical metadata store; crawlers, Glue APIs, SearchTables, Iceberg REST endpoint

artifacts.name: SageMaker Data Agent
artifacts.format: Notebooks and Query Editor; reads SageMaker Catalog business context. No stage label in the announcement

metrics.n: No governed metric object in the catalog. Glossary terms and metadata forms can describe a metric in text only.

dimensions.n: No dimension object. Glossary terms attach to assets and columns, but they define no hierarchies or grains.

relationships.n: No declared join or relationship object. Glossary terms can relate to other terms, which is not a data join.

synonyms.n: Glossary terms hold definitions, synonyms and related terms. Assets carry business names, descriptions, README text and metadata forms.

verifiedQueries.n: The catalog stores no question and SQL pairs. Redshift Q generative SQL custom context holds them instead.

nl2sql.n: SageMaker Data Agent reads catalog business context to write SQL and Python. It is a separate product and has no stage label.

ontology.n: Glossaries with related terms and metadata forms approximate business concepts. No object, link or action model.

graph.n: No graph query language in the catalog. Lineage shows as a graph in the UI. Neptune is a separate service.

vector.n: No vector or semantic search feature found in the catalog docs.

mcp.n: AWS documents no first-party MCP server for SageMaker Catalog. The AWS Data Processing MCP server manages Glue Data Catalog databases and tables.

governance.n: Publish and subscribe workflow, fine-grained access control, Lake Formation LF-Tags on Glue resources, and OpenLineage compatible lineage.

openStandard.n: Lineage accepts OpenLineage events, and Glue offers an Iceberg REST endpoint. No open semantic spec such as OSI.

aiDescriptions.n: Bedrock drafts business names, descriptions and glossary terms for Glue and custom assets. Reviewers accept or reject. Region limits and quotas apply.

bulkMetadata.n: StartMetadataGenerationRun and glossary, asset and data product APIs run in bulk. Glue UpdateTable sets table and column comments.

autoClassify.n: A Bedrock agent suggests glossary terms, including PII and PHI, from schema at publish time. Only a blog describes it.

sampleValues.n: No sample value or entity matching feature found in the catalog docs.

queryHistory.n: The catalog does not mine query history to suggest joins or metrics. Redshift Query Editor v2 uses history separately.

lineage.n: Column-level lineage from Glue, Redshift and Spark. It is OpenLineage compatible and has a PostLineageEvent API.

evals.n: No NL-to-SQL evaluation tooling in the catalog. A catalog export lets you query description coverage with SQL.

offers: A business glossary with terms, synonyms and related terms that you can link to assets and columns.
Bedrock drafts business names, descriptions and glossary terms for catalog assets.
Data products group assets with metadata and one access request path.
OpenLineage compatible lineage with a PostLineageEvent API for jobs outside AWS.
Daily export of asset metadata to an Iceberg table that SQL, Athena or an agent can query.
The Glue Data Catalog serves Iceberg REST clients and supports LF-Tags for attribute-based access.
gaps: No governed metric, dimension or join object. Business meaning stays in text fields.
AWS documents no first-party MCP server for the catalog.
AI recommendations cover limited Regions and have quotas. The default quota is 10,000 description runs a month.
No stored question and SQL pairs, sample value matching or query history mining in the catalog.
AI glossary classification for PII and PHI appears only in an AWS blog.
fillWith: Redshift Q generative SQL custom context
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Keep descriptions, glossary terms and lineage in SageMaker Catalog and build metrics in a separate layer such as dbt or Cube. Pass the catalog business context and curated question and SQL pairs to your agent, for example through Redshift custom context.

notes.text: Open source Unity Catalog (unitycatalog.io) is an Apache 2.0 server with an OpenAPI spec and an Iceberg REST API. Its docs list metric view tutorials but no AI comments, lineage or MCP server. The README calls it a Linux Foundation AI and Data sandbox project.
Databricks groups metric views, domains, Pages and certification flags as Unity Catalog semantics. Genie One uses them as the human-modeled layer of Genie Ontology. Pages are Beta.
Databricks-provided MCPs are Unity Catalog securables under system.ai, and Unity Gateway governs calls. The Genie One MCP is GA. The SQL, sandbox and web search MCPs need the Unity Gateway beta.
Snowflake describes Horizon Catalog as the agentic catalog, with Horizon Context as its governed context layer. Context collects, enriches and activates metadata for people, BI tools and agents.
The docs mark external engine access to Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables as GA. Write support (Mar 2026) and externally managed tables through Horizon (Aug 2026) have Preview release notes.
A catalog-linked database connects Snowflake to an external Iceberg REST catalog and syncs its tables. Snowflake names AWS Glue and Azure OneLake as examples.
SageMaker Catalog is built on Amazon DataZone, and the DataZone API reference still documents its APIs. The Glue Data Catalog is a separate technical metadata store that SageMaker Catalog reads.

AWS announced in June 2026 that SageMaker Data Agent reads catalog glossary terms, metadata forms and README text. The announcement says the business context can sync from Collibra, Atlan and Alation.
